articleTitle: The Influence of AI Apps on Enhancing Mathematics Learning Among Primary Education Students
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The influence of artificial intelligence (AI) applications on enhancing mathematics learning in primary school students exhibits a growing trend in academic performance. These applications, along with the use of mobile devices, offer personalized tools tailored to the students' needs, enabling them to effectively improve their mathematical skills. Furthermore, the improvement can be significant, provided that an appropriate application is selected, effectively implemented in the classroom, and proper monitoring of student progress is conducted. The instant feedback and interactive resources provided by AI apps contribute to more dynamic and efficient learning and technology in mathematics for primary school students in Peru.

articleTitle: Relation Between Learning Styles and Academic Performance: A Study in Peruvian Health Students in the Context of Digital Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The identification and consideration of learning styles in the current context of digital transformation in university education implies in the need to adapt teaching methods to the characteristics and preferences of students in the digital age. The aim of this study was to determine the relationship between learning styles and academic performance in health sciences students at a private Peruvian university in the context of digital transformation. For this purpose, a basic research methodology with a quantitative approach, non-experimental design, cross-sectional and correlational descriptive level was used. The sample was composed for 110 students in the first semester of health sciences school from a private peruvian university who responded to the Honey and Alonso learning styles test (CHAEA) to measure the learning styles variable (LS), while to measure the academic performance variable the academic record was used. Spearman's Rho statistic was used for the correlation test. The results showed that the most frequent style was the theorist style (68.2% for high and very high levels), a greater frequency of well-achieved learning (71.8%), and the absence of a significant relationship between learning styles and academic performance (Active LS: p=0.318; Reflective LS: p=0.648; Theoretical LS: p=0.763). It was concluded that there is no meaningful relationship between learning styles and academic performance in health sciences students.

articleTitle: Selection of the Best AI Educational Tool Applied to University-Level Teaching and Learning Process Using the AHP Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The implementation of technology in university education is essential for students to develop comprehensive learning in an environment that can become routine without constant motivation. This study seeks to find an objective approach that can serve as a guide to identify the best Artificial Intelligence educational tool for learning development. In this paper, extensive research was conducted using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) method. Four AI educational tools were proposed and compared: learning platforms, virtual assistants, virtual reality, and Chat GPT. These technologies were evaluated based on key criteria such as flexibility, cohesion, adaptability, and transformation. The final selection was made with the active participation of four specialized experts. The results revealed that the best AI educational tool is Chat GPT.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Curricular Management Support Tool for the Quality Systems of the Engineering Programs at Uniandes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The School of Engineering at University of Los Andes offers nine accredited undergraduate programs recognized by the Colombian National Accreditation Council (CNA) and the Accreditation Board of Engineering and Technology (ABET). To enhance the quality systems, the School initiated a pilot proj ect using the uAssessment tool from uPlanner as a curricular management support tool of each program. Starting in 2022, the Atenea Committee adjusted the tool to meet the programs' needs and integrated it with the University's systems. By 2024–1, Environmental and Civil Engineering programs began trials and included information of 2023–2 of their quality systems, followed by Biomedical Engineering. By 2024, other programs have started to conduct their trials generating different types of reports. This process involved extensive collaboration and weekly meetings to refine the tool and align it with the School's quality requirements. This tool facilitates decision-making by providing comprehensive visualizations of quality system results and encourages the use of Bloque Neon among instructors. The initiative's success relied on continuous improvement efforts and addressing cultural resistance to new technologies. The ongoing transformation aims to expand the tool adoption across the School of Engineering and then across the University.

articleTitle: Internship Performance of Chemical Engineering Students in Cusco, Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The internship performance of Chemical Engineering students at the National University of San Antonio Abad (UNSAAC) in Cusco, Peru was analyzed. The study population was students who carried out their internships during the academic semesters 2022- I, 2022- II, 2023–1, and 2023-11; In addition, the following components were considered within the evaluation: sex, companies where they carried out their internships, sector or field, and supervisor evaluation. The data were analyzed using the free statistical software R, obtaining that more than half of the students carry out their internships in the food industry, 51 %, followed by the environmental and industrial safety sector with 21 % and 6% respectively, in less proportion with mining, research and materials industry sectors with 2%, 2%, and 1 % respectively. The student sex was mostly of men, 69%, and 52% of women, reported during this study period. In addition, 1452 student ratings by their supervisors were evaluated, where students achieved a rating of 17.77 on average, on a scale from 0 to 20, considering a standard deviation of 1.11, and a variability coefficient of 0.06. In general, they were doing well during stage in enterprises; however, there were some recommendations from supervisors about student performance; for example, they should improve punctuality, communication and teamwork skills.

articleTitle: The PBL Methodology in a Hybrid Class in an Integrative Systems Engineering Course
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The educational process is enriched when transformed to merge creativity, collaboration, knowledge, and expression into a student-centered teaching-learning plan that transcends traditional classroom boundaries. The present study aims to present the experience of a learning session applying the active project-based learning (PBL) methodology, where 50 systems and computer engineering students presented 15 educational chatbot projects. In the project's development, the SCRUM project management framework was used as the course lasted eight weeks. The project guidelines were provided at the beginning of class after elaborating on an activity guide (responsibilities of the teacher and student, guides, presentations, and activities). The results were the participation of the students in developing the educational chatbot projects in the course and developing soft and hard skills through teamwork and presentations. It is concluded that the PBL methodology allows students to participate actively and collaboratively in the Virtual Classroom according to their abilities and skills to achieve the objective set; thus, the university prepares the students with the necessary competencies for their graduation, allowing them to perform effectively in the world of work because they learn to develop projects in real situations. The proper incorporation of the active PBL methodology in the virtual course of Project Workshop 2 contributed to the student's achievement of learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Model for Predicting the Achievement of the Graduate Profile Through Academic Performance in University Students
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The profile of the graduate allows to understand the objective of training during the teaching-learning process in the higher educational institutions, which, in turn, shows the competences acquired by the students. In order to predict the achievement of the captured profile, the present research sought to implement a model in machine learning to predict the achievement of the profile of the graduate in the students of the Faculty of Systems Engineering of the National University of the Center of Peru (hereinafter nominated as FIS-UNCP), having as input indicators academic performance. The research was carried out following the scientific method, of a quantitative approach, explanatory-predictive level, where the design was nonexperimental longitudinal trend, the chosen population took into account the 355 students of the FIS-UNCP enrolled during the 2023-II academic semester. After the investigation, the result was obtained that the predictive model presents a 97.50% accuracy in the forecasts, with a specificity of 100%, evidencing that the model succeeds in predicting the achievement of the profile of the graduate having as inputs to the indicators of the academic performance of the students. In conclusion, with a T-value=3.239 and P-value=0.001, it can be stated that academic performance significantly influences the achievement of the graduate profile based on a prediction model with machine learning in FIS-UNCP students.

articleTitle: Impact of ANEAES Accreditation on the Computer Engineering Program at Universidad Americana
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Since its initial evaluation by the National Agency for Higher Education Evaluation and Accreditation (ANEAES), the Computer Engineering program at American University has implemented continuous improvements based on the Improvement Plan. These improvements focus on five key dimensions: governance, academic project, human resources, resources and results, and impact. This paper discusses the improvements made in these areas. Universidad Americana adjusted the organizational structure, updated curricula and bibliographies, implemented the Human Talent Management Portal, renewed laboratory equipment, and promoted participation in research programs. The results show that accreditation has strengthened the organizational structure, optimized resource management, improved the quality of the teaching-learning process and increased the quality of professional training. In conclusion, ANEAES accreditation has been fundamental for the development and consolidation of the Computer Engineering program at Universidad Americana, positioning it as a reference in the training of highly qualified professionals in the field of computer engineering.

articleTitle: Impact of ANEAES Accreditations on the Continuous Improvement of the Production Systems Engineering Degree Program at the Polytechnic Faculty of the National University of Asunción
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This work analyzes the impact of the National Agency for Higher Education Evaluation and Accreditation (ANEAES) accreditations on the continuous improvement of the Production Systems Engineering degree program at the Polytechnic Faculty of the National University of Asunción. The academic quality evaluation model in Paraguay, regulated by ANEAES, establishes that an improvement plan must be implemented once a degree is accredited. This model was applied to the Production Systems Engineering degree, using the Deming cycle (plan, execute, verify, and act) to guide the development and implementation of the improvement plan from 2020 to 2023. Through this accreditation process and the implementation of the improvement plan, several areas of improvement were identified and worked on. The evaluations carried out with different instruments demonstrated that the program has implemented effective actions that have solidified the quality of its educational offer in higher education. The accreditation and the corresponding improvement plan have allowed the Production Systems Engineering degree not only to comply with predefined quality standards, but also to foster a culture of continuous improvement. This has resulted in a more robust educational offer adapted to the demands and changes of the environment.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality to Support the Teaching-Learning Process in Computer Graphics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: In this research, we analyze the impact of the use of augmented reality (AR) during computer graphics course. First, modeling sessions were conducted using Unity and Vuforia, and linked to the course subjects. Then, a questionnaire was applied to measure the motivation to the course and its future applications, the importance of augmented reality in the course and in their professional education. As a result, 64% of students considered AR is extremely or very important in the practical part, 61% of students considered AR inclusion in the teaching-learning process was extremely or very important, 70% of students considered the use of Vuforia is extremely or very beneficial in their education, 66% of students are extremely or very motivated about the use of computer graphics in AR and 70% of students are extremely or very motivated to develop current applications using. That indicates AR inclusion was important to get student attention and motivation.

articleTitle: AI Ethics in the Fields of Education and Research: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence tools and their integration into various societal sectors have introduced significant ethical challenges. This research focuses on identifying the most frequently discussed ethical aspects of AI within the realms of education and research. A systematic literature review, supported by AI-driven tools, was conducted to address this objective. The study reveals that key ethical aspects recurrently examined include transparency and explainability, privacy and data protection, responsibility and accountability, and equity. Transparency and explainability are crucial for ensuring that AI systems in education operate in a comprehensible manner, fostering trust among educators and students. Privacy and data protection emphasize the importance of handling personal data with utmost care, adhering to relevant regulations. Responsibility and accountability highlight the need for clear mechanisms for overseeing AI deployment, while equity addresses the avoidance of bias and discrimination. The findings underscore the necessity of addressing a broad spectrum of ethical considerations throughout the lifecycle of AI systems to promote their responsible use in educational and research settings.

articleTitle: Prediction of Labor Insertion in Graduates Based on the Pre-Professional Internship Process Through a Supervised Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This research sought to implement a predictive model using machine learning algorithms to determine if a student graduated from the Faculty of Systems Engineering of the National University of Central Peru (hereinafter FIS-UNCP) is able to enter the world of work taking into account employers and competences during the pre-professional internship process. The research was carried out following the scientific-systemic method, of a quantitative approach, of applied type and explanatory-predictive level, where the design was nonexperimental longitudinal trend, the chosen population took into account the 355 students of the FIS-UNCP which managed to complete the pre professional internship process from 2023-I to the present. The results showed that the predictive model had an assertiveness of 92.96% allowing to efficiently predict the employment of graduates taking into account the process of pre professional practices, with a T-value = 22.909 and P-value = 0.000, evidencing that the pre professional internship process significantly influences the employment insertion of graduates of the FIS UNCP through a predictive model supervised in machine learning.

articleTitle: Visual and External Auditory in Information Retention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This article aims at finding the influence between the visual and external auditory stimuli in information retention. For this purpose, a sample of engineering students, who voluntarily accepted to take part in the experiment, was used. Through a 2k experimental design of 16 treatments with 2 replicates per treatment, the data collection among the sample of engineering students took place. Then, the results were tabulated and processed. These show that the external stimuli do influence information retention.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing: Exploring the Digital Frontier for the Academic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The cloud is everywhere, but what does it represent, how does it exist? - that is a question people may ask themselves at this present time. The effort here is to go in-depth about how the cloud revolutionizes our realm of technology. We utilize Amazon AWS to display different usages of the cloud such as storage, coding websites with HTML, hosting of websites, and usage of virtual machines within a personal cloud server. Using virtual machines, we display how the services are used for cloud computing. Cloud storage allows for the viewing and saving of these applications and software. The cloud allows for the usage of these applications which handle many different purposes, the most famous being AI and Cybersecurity. These functions and services the cloud provides, top companies utilize them as well, and we illustrate the use in an academic environment.

articleTitle: How to Improve Graduate Attributes Attainment with Virtual Reality: A Case Study in Industrial Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This document explores the integration of Virtual Reality (VR) in engineering education, highlighting its potential to enhance graduate attributes attainment through innovative learning methods, while delving into the importance of STEM knowledge and developing essential skills for future engineers. The proposal advocates for a project-oriented approach where students work on Capstone Projects. These projects require collaboration and mobilization of resources, allowing students to apply their technical knowledge in real-world contexts while developing a range of specific skills categorized into technical (hard skills) and interpersonal (soft skills). The results are not conclusive regarding competencies attainment; however, preliminary findings are promising to concern the use of VR in Capstone Projects. In the blended learning modality, competency attainment rose by 1.0% to 13.0%. In contrast, in the face-to-face modality, the improvement ranged from 1.3% to 19.8%. More experiments are needed with a large number of students to evaluate its impact on learning experiences.

articleTitle: The Deployment of Virtualized Operating Systems to Reveal Network Vulnerabilities for Classroom Setting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Virtualization has grown as a modular system that allows individuals and companies to perform security tests. Virtualization allows a host or physical device to create partitions that can contain multiple Virtual Machines (VMs). These Virtual Machines can manage different operating systems to run in isolated environments. In this paper, our work deals with hypervisors including Hyper-V, VirtualBox, and VMware Workstation to seek vulnerabilities in systems utilizing tools built into Linux-based systems to detect malicious network traffic. The Honeypot tool from Pentbox denies access from potential attackers attempting to access to your device through open ports. Our methodology employs tools inherent to Linux-based systems, such as Nmap for scanning and evaluating network vulnerabilities, alongside analyzing network traffic for malicious activities. We have deployed the Netstat command to log incoming and outgoing network packets to reveal Network Vulnerabilities in a classroom setting.

articleTitle: Automated Prototype for Demonstrating the Properties of Gases in Natural Science Laboratories
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This article focuses on the creation of an automated device for the natural science chemistry laboratories at Universidad Popular del Cesar. This prototype is designed to facilitate the demonstration and verification of the properties of gases, specifically Boyle-Mariotte and Charles laws, in a more efficient and precise manner. Utilizing a microcontrolled system and various sensors to measure pressure, temperature, and volume, the prototype allows for automated experiments, reducing preparation and execution time while ensuring accurate and consistent data. The development of the software and firmware enables communication between the system components, and a graphical interface facilitates real-time visualization of the variables. The tests conducted validated the prototype's effectiveness and reliability, providing a tool that optimizes laboratory time and enhances students' understanding and interest in natural sciences, making the learning process more dynamic and motivating.

articleTitle: Ethical Challenges in the Teaching of Specialized Subjects in the Training of Industrial Engineers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Ethics in industrial engineering education is of utmost importance. Delving into the specific ethical challenges of careers provides valuable information for the training of future responsible professionals. Several relevant characteristics define responsible behavior for aspiring industrial engineers, shaped by their professional training. In this sense, Industrial engineers must internalize ethical principles—honesty, integrity, transparency, and respect for others. These principles guide decision making in the design, production and management of industrial systems. Furthermore, they must understand that CSR is crucial. Companies must contribute to social well-being. Industrial engineers must understand how business decisions impact communities, employees, and stakeholders. Issues such as equity, diversity, human rights and fair labor relations fall within this scope. Engineers must understand organizational dynamics from a governance perspective. Decision-making, accountability and transparency play essential roles. Contributing to greater efficiency and ethical business management is part of an engineer's responsibility. Researchers recognize the need for statistical tools to gauge Industrial Engineering students' appreciation of these ethical aspects. Two critical axes—‘Social and Economic Impact’ and ‘Communication and Collaboration’—are integral to the ethical framework. Empathy and active listening skills are essential to understanding the diverse needs of stakeholders. That is why the main objective is to see to what extent these skills or strengths that the career intends to provide in training, are taken by students, mainly in specialty courses; and based on the results obtained, establish what measures are going to be taken to strengthen the need for identity between the purpose sought by the curriculum, in response to what has been forged by the various interest groups, and the understanding, application and practice by the students, with the aim of being able to establish an improvement in the application of these strengths with a view to the search for a transformation with a social and development, based on ethics as the fundamental axis of professional consolidation.

articleTitle: Characteristics of University Happiness Conditions and Academic Performance: A Case Study of a University in Arequipa, Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The analysis reveals that university students' happiness, particularly in aspects of well-being, community, and perspective, positively correlates with academic performance. Women exhibit slightly higher levels of happiness compared to men. Satisfaction in areas such as recreational activities and social relationships also influences happiness. However, students display a high ecological footprint, indicating an “environmental distraction.” It is crucial to enhance psychological well-being and sustainability in educational policies.

articleTitle: Educational Model to Develop Work Skills in Students at a Higher Education Institute in Lima, Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The present research aims to propose an educational model to develop work skills in students of a technological institute in Metropolitan Lima, for which it is framed in the qualitative approach, with an educational design applied within the framework of the naturalistic and interpretive paradigm. For the research, a sample of 25 students was worked with; from the regular training program of the technical careers of the institute taken into account for the research, as well as five teachers and five representatives of the companies that constantly request students, to whom the questionnaire was applied, as well as the observation and interview guide. In the field diagnosis, it was found that the evaluated companies consider that the students have an optimal level of work skills in general terms; however, there are some social skills that need to be reinforced and improved. On the other hand, it was also obtained as a result that the educational model must be updated according to the needs of the current student profile, as well as the labor demands. The teachers have an active participation in the development of the skills of their students, which enables them to be their referents. The proposed educational model is composed of methodological dimensions: philosophical dimension, academic dimension and organizational dimension; in addition to transversal components such as contextual adaptation, disruptive teachers, project-based learning and globalization, and all of this in an articulated manner allows this proposed educational model to have greater solidity in the formation of the work skills of its students.

articleTitle: Social Dimension of the Evaluative Culture of Learning and Student Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This research seeks to establish the relationship between the perception of the social dimension of the culture of teaching evaluation and its relationship with the satisfaction of students at a private university in Lima. It is a crosscutting, descriptive and correlational research with a non-experimental quantitative approach. The methodological design consisted of selecting a representative sample of students and carrying out the collection and analysis of information using two validated instruments. The result was that there was a positive correlation between the proposed variables, that is, that the greater the perception of the social dimension of the evaluative culture, the higher the student's satisfaction. Similarly, statistical evidence suggests that there is an average relationship between the perception of the social dimension of the evaluative culture of learning and student satisfaction at a private university in Lima (0,000 ≤ 0.05).

articleTitle: Analysis of Student Facial Reactions During Classroom Instruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This study seeks to construct a model that is capable of categorizing students' facial expressions during classroom instructional sessions. Facial expressions serve as pivotal non-verbal indicators, offering valuable insights into students' emotional and cognitive conditions. Leveraging Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) technology, this research integrates image models with facial geometry feature models to identify a range of facial expressions including happiness, sadness, neutrality, surprise, anger, and fatigue. The dataset utilized in this investigation comprises 2,069 facial images sorted into six distinct categories of facial expressions. Data collection was carried out through the recording of primary school educational sessions and monitoring of classroom footage sourced from YouTube. Subsequent to preliminary processing steps, encompassing facial landmark recognition, geometry feature extraction, normalization, and data enhancement, the dataset was partitioned into training, validation, and testing sets utilizing an 80:10:10 ratio. The constructed CNN model incorporates six convolutional layers for facial images and four fully connected layers for facial geometry features. Model assessment was conducted utilizing metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results from testing reveal that the proposed model exhibits considerable accuracy in recognizing students' facial expressions, with a validation accuracy rate of 92% and a testing accuracy rate of 95%. This research makes a notable contribution to the fields of education and psychology by furnishing valuable feedback on students' emotional and cognitive involvement, thereby supporting educators in pinpointing learning impediments and enhancing instructional methods.

articleTitle: Educational Software for Learning Load Profile in Residential Supplies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This paper presents the results of the development and implementation of an educational program in Matlab® for students enrolled in the course Introduction to Electrical Engineering and related areas. The principal objective of the program is to enable students to recognize the significance of their role as electrical engineers in the context of sustainable societal development, through the interpretation of the load profile of any residential supply, which is a crucial aspect of energy efficiency and resource management. To achieve this objective, the software generates graphical representations of the instantaneous power and daily electrical energy demand of a residential property. The methodology employed entails an exhaustive record of the installed power in the house, obtained through an inventory of all electrical appliances in operation, with consideration given to their specific active power. Furthermore, a comprehensive record of the frequency of daily appliance usage is maintained, segmented into 30-minute intervals. The results of the analysis demonstrate that the utilization of the Perfilcargafv software markedly enhances the students' capacity to analyze and interpret the load profile, thereby facilitating their theoretical and practical comprehension of the subject matter and enabling them to discern energy efficiency strategies. In conclusion, the educational software developed has the dual benefit of improving the learning process in the field of electrical engineering and fostering awareness of the importance of energy efficiency and sustainable development among future professionals in the sector.

articleTitle: BITA: The First Female Robotics Intercollegiate Championship to Foster STEM Attitudes and Skills
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This article presents the design, development and results obtained from a robotics female intercollegiate competition designed to promote STEM attitudes, seeking to deconstruct the social imaginaries that keep girls and adolescents away from choosing a career in STEM areas. The experience was developed around a space adventure as a central activity and theme, for which the participants were not only prepared in the technical skills and scientific knowledge necessary for their successful performance, but also developed a process of diagnosis and intervention on some of the socio-cultural factors that influence the moment of choosing a professional career, particularly in science, technology or engineering. The results showed that although some of the participants already had genuine interests in pursuing a STEM career, the experience allowed them to strengthen those interests and, in other cases, to reorient their career choices. The championship also proved to be an excellent alternative for integrating the students' families and teachers in the process of empowering and increasing girls' levels of self-efficacy and self-confidence to pursue careers historically dominated by men.

articleTitle: Gamified and Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Knowledge Base in a Social Platform for Self-Learning in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a technical model for a self-learning platform in higher education that integrates gamification, artificial intelligence, an online knowledge base, and a social network. Using WordPress as the central platform, specific tools such as GamiPress, AI Engine, BuddyPress, and BetterDocs are evaluated. Unlike previous studies, this work uniquely combines these technologies to address specific challenges in higher education, such as student engagement and personalized learning. Through an exhaustive literature review and a rigorous comparison of available plugins, it is argued that WordPress is a viable option for implementing this solution. This study provides a solid foundation for future implementations and empirical evaluations, presenting evidence on the effectiveness of integrating these tools in enhancing self-directed education.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Model for the Improvement of the Quality of Education at the National University of Central Peru, Huancayo 2024
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This paper presents a project that addresses the problem of the high rate of non-attendance and disinterest in the tutoring course, and how this affects academic performance. The objective is to determine the influence of implementing an Artificial Intelligence Model using data prediction and intelligent tutoring. The hypothesis is that this model will positively influence the improvement of students' educational quality. A model was developed in SmartPLS using a dataset obtained from an application developed in Flutter and trained in Azure Machine Learning. The results show the reliability of the data through Cronbach's Alpha (0.747 to 0.975), explanatory power of the model through the R-squared (0.001 to 0.188), good prediction accuracy through the path coefficient (0.022 to 0.433), and adequate statistical significance through the p-value=0.000.

articleTitle: Intelligent Computational Architecture for Improving the Quality of Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent computational architecture designed to enhance the quality of higher education in an academic ecosystem. By integrating generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), complex systems, and blockchain technology, this architecture aims to invigorate formative research and optimize educational processes. The proposed architecture seeks to facilitate effective collaboration and enhance educational quality by modeling academic ecosystems as complex networks and using smart contracts for intellectual property management, coupled with the incorporation of participation incentives through blockchain-based social tokens. The resulting architecture employs autonomous agents to propose projects and automatically recruit participants by combining complex networks with GenAI, preserving intellectual property via blockchain and managing incentives with social tokens.

articleTitle: Relationship Between Internal Communication and Resistance to Change in the Teaching Staff of an Educational Company
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to find out the relationship between, internal communication, and resistance to change. A sample of teachers from a private educational institution in the District of Lima - Peru; based on the theoretical reference of Formanchuck (2008), whose validity Conceptual is fulfilled, by verifying in the thesis of the last five years and the numbering of the advantages and disadvantages of the dimensions of internal communication, essential, operational, strategic, evaluative, motivational, learning and intelligence. Along with this theory, the model of Lorenzo (2000) assumed, which establishes the logical, psychological, and sociological dimensions of resistance to change. The assumption was that internal communication correlates with the resignations of resistance to change: for this purpose, the Internal Communication and resistance to change questionnaires were applied to a sample of 116 teachers. The type of study of the roach was quantitative, by the correlational descriptive level, because we will obtain important characteristics of each variable in the reality studied and the knowledge of the intensity and direction of the correlation between the variable communication and resistance to change. The hypothetical deductive method as soon as we start from theories as general references to verify its occurrence in a specific situation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Student Retention: Action Research on First-Year Pedagogical Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: According to the Education Data Initiative, 24.1% of undergraduate first-year students have a 12-month dropout rate, making it the highest compared to the remaining years of higher education. External factors in the Southern Hemisphere such as household's income level, lack of enough public institutions, or gender inequality led to gaps in enrolment rates in higher education that can reach over 60 percentage points when comparing the richest and poorest countries. Our research-action-based pedagogical strategies target first-year students at a private Peruvian university serving low-and middle-income families. The primary objective is to accurately assess students' skills, needs, and expectations as they begin their higher education journey, and to address these effectively. We've selected a first-semester course that not only imparts fundamental skills for future studies but also introduces students to key aspects of their chosen field, ultimately enabling informed career decisions. By identifying and addressing students' primary concerns, we aim to develop more effective dropout prevention policies. Throughout this process, quality assurance plays a crucial role in ensuring that our strategies are implemented consistently, evaluated rigorously, and continually improved. This focus on quality helps maintain high standards in our educational approach, enhances student satisfaction, and contributes to better retention rates. This pilot study in two Building Materials classes employed problem-based learning strategies, emphasizing real-life scenarios and research-action problems. The aim was to improve student retention and enhance the first-year university experience. Results showed lower dropout rates, increased student motivation, and higher faculty satisfaction. The approach fostered student autonomy and engagement, suggesting PBL's effectiveness in supporting student success in higher education.

articleTitle: Learning Chemistry Through Controversy? Reading Discrepant Perspectives to Promote Comprehension, Multiple Text Integration, and Epistemic Emotions in Freshmen Engineering Students
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Reading comprehension plays a key role in STEM education, since its association with developing communication skills, critical thinking, and integrating multiple perspectives, among other scientific skills. This work presents an intervention embedded within a college course in General Chemistry, to examine performance in a multiple text reading task associated with a curricular topic (influence of diet on body pH). One-hundred and eighteen students participated voluntarily (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{M}=\mathbf{19}$</tex> years, 47% female, 53% male). The sample was split into two groups, one read about the topic from discrepant texts and the other from concordant texts. The intervention included reading the texts (discrepant or not), writing an essay, self-reporting the emotions experienced during the activity (epistemic emotions), and answering comprehension questions. The results showed significant differences in the three outcomes, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{p} <. \mathbf{05}$</tex>. The group that read the discrepant texts showed better performance in literal comprehension, a greater likelihood of producing intertextual integration in the essays, and higher levels of surprise and curiosity, compared to the group that read the texts in the concordant condition.

articleTitle: Assessing Soft Skills Development in Informatics Students Through Project-Based Learning and Agile Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: In the current dynamic and competitive job market, influenced by the rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence, Soft skills have become increasingly valuable. Similarly, today's informatics labor sector requires collaboration, ethics, and adaptability. However, traditional education often prioritizes technical skills over others. Thus, the present study aims to assess the development of soft skills in informatics students using the Project Based Learning (PBL) methodology within the context of Agile frameworks: Scrum and Kanban. A mixed-method study was designed using both quantitative and qualitative approaches. Student outcomes based on ICACIT accreditation criteria were utilized to quantitatively assess soft skills, focusing on indicators such as teamwork, communication, professionalism, and ethics. A perception survey was conducted to qualitatively gather data on students' experiences in developing soft skills. The results indicate a positive academic performance, with achievement levels exceeding 70%. Students also reported favorable perceptions of acquiring soft skills, and there was a significant correlation between quantitative and qualitative findings. Lastly, the assessment shows that implementing PBL within agile frameworks positively impacted informatics students, especially in communication and teamwork skills.

articleTitle: Key Competencies for Industry 5.0 in Undergraduate Engineering Students
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Core competencies have a vital role to enable a sustainable change towards Industry 5.0. In view of this, the study aims to characterize the university training skills for adaptation to Industry 5.0 of engineering students at the National University Toribio Rodriguez de Mendoza of Amazonas (UNTRM). It was a descriptive, non-experimental quantitative research; the study population was made up of students and professors of engineering majors, with a sample of 138 students and 28 professors. The results show, that engineering students possess high levels of competencies related to Industry 5.0, including critical thinking (71.7%), creativity (69.6%), digital competencies (61.6%), resilience (60.9%), ethics and collaboration (69.6%). These results are the consequence of innovative pedagogical strategies implemented by teachers, who integrate methodologies that foster advanced thinking, technological adaptability and ethical awareness, thus preparing future engineers for the challenges of a rapidly evolving world.

articleTitle: CS2023 Curricula Guidelines and Computer Science Accreditation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Periodically, since 1968 [1], a model curriculum for computer science has been published. The most recent curriculum guidelines are CS2023 [2] which update the previous CS2013 guidelines [3]. CS2023 has also moved toward a discussion of professional dispositions and competencies in addition to a knowledge-based guideline. Accreditation agencies for computer science may require specific curriculum content in their accreditation criteria and consequently may need to consider criteria changes to align with the model curriculum guidelines. This paper examines the changes from CS2013 to CS2023, and considers what impact it may have on accreditation criteria in the future.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Student Desertion in Electronic Engineering at UPTC and UdeC Between 2015 and 2018
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Accreditation of Engineering and Computing Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This document reports the most common economic, social and academic causes of student dropout in Electronic Engineering programs at the Universidad de Cundinamarca and the Universidad Pedagógica y Tecnológica de Colombia for academic periods 2015 and 2018. The purpose of this analysis is to identify and socialize the results obtained so that these universities generate prevention strategies against academic desertion. A comparative analysis between two non-probabilistic random samples of students was carried out by applying structured interviews and opinion questionnaires. It was proposed to infer the relationships of similarity or difference between the causes of desertion present in the two samples. As a result, it was found that 83.6% of the deserting population were men; 26.47<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of the students belong to an economic stratum 3; 47.05% of the students come from cities other than the University headquarters; and 38.8% of desertions are due to failing a subject three consecutive times. In addition, 27.77% failed the subjects with an arithmetic mean lower than 3.0. In general, the most common causes of desertion are academic. In addition, electronic engineering programs have been developing strategies to reduce student dropout rates and increase retention rates. It is also proposed that the programs intensify teacher training activities in aspects of teaching methodologies and pedagogy.
